title: Placing Abstract Interfaces and Concrete Implementations in the Same Package
pattern: An abstract boundary interface and its concrete, technology-specific implementations reside within the same compilation unit or package boundary.
why_bad: Fails to enforce a strict architecture boundary. Developers can easily bypass the interface and instantiate or directly depend on the concrete repository, coupling the client code to infrastructure details.
detection: Trait/interface definitions and their concrete implementations (such as database-backed structs) located within the same package or module.
counterexample: Very small libraries where no separate architectural layers exist. Marked as `Contextual`.
source: Martin Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* (2002), "Separated Interface", p. 311, 466.
